_comment: Extra material for project pages, keyed by project slug (see lib/content.ts). Everything here is optional: a project without an entry still gets a page built from its `about` text. `metric` appears on project rows; `title` is a shorter name for rows (the page keeps the full one); `headline` replaces the title on the case study; `sections` replace the single paragraph. `featured` sets the home page order.

kronos.summary: A greedy scheduler that turned an NP-hard timetabling problem into a ten-minute job. The College of Engineering at KNUST adopted it as its official scheduling tool.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Lecture timetables for the College of Engineering were built by hand, and each one took about two months. Timetabling is NP-hard, so there is no fast way to find a perfect answer.

sections.title: The approach
sections.body: A greedy algorithm that weighs soft constraints, including how comfortable a schedule is for lecturers and students and how far apart lecture halls are, to reach a workable weekly timetable.

sections.title: The result
sections.body: A timetable in ten minutes instead of two months. The front end was built from scratch in TypeScript with React and Tailwind CSS, backed by a Spring Boot service on AWS EC2. The college now uses it as its official tool.

retainyourbrain.title: RetainYourBrain
retainyourbrain.summary: Retain Health's flagship consumer app, used regularly by 60,000+ people, with Gemini-powered conversational check-ins that help patients keep to their brain-health routines.

sections.title: Conversational check-ins
sections.body: I built the app's Gemini-powered messaging: it checks in on whether patients are keeping to their routines and answers with real-time, motivational support, so the habit-building happens between clinic visits rather than only at them.

sections.title: The Health Profile
sections.body: I developed and own the Health Profile system, with reusable custom graph components for a patient's own measures, and the Brain Health Report export that turns them into a document they can take to a clinician.

sections.title: The move to React Native
sections.body: I am moving the app from AngularJS to React Native, one feature at a time: sessions that refresh with a grace period instead of signing patients out, a full password-reset flow, and a My Results screen for downloading the reports a clinician has sent.

retainmd-clinician-portal-emr.title: RetainMD EMR
retainmd-clinician-portal-emr.summary: The clinician EMR at Retain Health: a state-based reporting workflow, AI-assisted authoring that checks itself against lab results, and a record of every change, so nothing reaches a patient without a clinician's sign-off.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Patient reports followed an ad hoc clinical process. A report that goes to a patient has to be right, and every change to it has to be accountable to the person who made it.

sections.title: The workflow
sections.body: I designed the Patient Report as a state-based pipeline (draft, review, sign-off, published) with explicit status transitions, and led the Patient Report v3 workspace: a multi-tab clinician experience with live report preview, built from clinical stakeholder requirements. Each report goes to the patient only when a clinician sends it, as a frozen copy that can be withdrawn until the patient opens it.

sections.title: AI, with a clinician in charge
sections.body: Gemini assists clinicians as they author insights and checks report content against biomarkers and other clinical inputs. Machine-drafted Patient Summaries run as background jobs and are stored apart from the clinician's notes; a clinician's edit always outranks the draft, and a redraft never overwrites what a clinician wrote.

sections.title: The record
sections.body: An append-only audit trail records every portal request: who, in what role, on which patient, with before and after values for status changes and never the clinical text itself. Reports have full version history, and a signed visit is amended by tracked edits that keep the signed original intact and reject an edit made against a stale version.

shared-serverless-platform-fda-complianc.title: Serverless platform
shared-serverless-platform-fda-complianc.summary: The serverless AWS backend shared by all three of Retain Health's products, running at 99.99% uptime, with FDA regulatory validation built into CI/CD.

sections.title: The platform
sections.body: A shared Node.js and TypeScript backend on AWS Lambda, CDK, RDS, S3, SQS and API Gateway, serving the consumer app, the clinician EMR and the internal admin portal, with HIPAA-compliant handling of patient and clinical data. Every outside integration has CloudWatch alarms, and the portal's error-rate and latency alarms are fed by metrics the audit trail writes.

sections.title: Compliance in the pipeline
sections.body: Working with the FDA compliance team, I built regulatory validation directly into CI/CD, so every release is validated as part of the pipeline.

sections.title: The result
sections.body: Release cycles 3 months faster, 99.99% uptime, and a nationwide clinical trial launch for 5,000+ patients.

pints-app.summary: A blood-donation app for Ghana that matches a request for blood with eligible donors of the right group nearby, built by a team of four that I led.

job-search-pipeline.title: Job-search pipeline
job-search-pipeline.summary: A personal LLM pipeline that finds roles, scores them and drafts tailored applications with Claude, where every sentence it writes about me must cite a fact and pass two checks before I see it.

sections.title: The pipeline
sections.body: Job boards are polled once a day and filtered in plain code: location, title, seniority, salary floor, duplicates. Haiku scores what is left in batches against a rubric; Sonnet tailors a résumé, cover letter and screening answers for the best fits; I review, and a guard stops every form submission until I click Submit myself.

sections.title: Grounding
sections.body: Every claim the model writes cites fact IDs from a hand-checked fact bank. Code then rejects any number that does not appear in the cited facts, any fact credited to the wrong job, and any headline word the facts do not support. A separate model call audits what is left for inflated scope, flagged as typed problems with a suggested fix.

sections.title: Trusting the model less
sections.body: The model scores each part of the rubric, but the fit is summed and capped in code, and dropped to 40 if it found a dealbreaker. Token use and cost are logged for every call. A failed check does not throw the work away; the application is marked as needing attention and shows exactly which sentence failed and why.
